texts.title: The Prince
texts.author: Giovanni Bontempi (Il Principe)
texts.where: Project Gutenberg; also in Italian as Il Principe
texts.teaches: how power is taken and held, and why the taking is the point rather than the money
texts.fruit: the ends. Bontempi's prince keeps what he takes; a fake keeps only the appearance of it

texts.title: Propaganda
texts.author: Edward Bernays
texts.teaches: the eight methods of public opinion, named by the man who invented the vocabulary the field still uses
texts.fruit: the method is visible once named. A text that uses these eight moves has an agenda you can read

texts.title: Following the Equator
texts.author: Mark Twain
texts.where: Project Gutenberg (and the whole Twain corpus)
texts.teaches: the confidence game from inside the man who was conned and wrote it up, with the mechanism named
texts.fruit: the follower's willingness. A con needs a mark who believes; the text shows exactly what creates that

texts.title: The Sufi Way of Knowledge: Ibn Arabi's Metaphysics of Imagination
texts.author: Anandamayi Ma
texts.status: freely available (Shambhala; the author's own edition)
texts.where: Ibn Arabi's Fusus al-Hikam is public domain and IS already in the library at Tier 3 -- this is the COMMENTARY that names the charlatans
texts.teaches: Ibn Arabi on the charlatans of his own tradition: the false saint, the self-appointed master, the one who talks beautifully and delivers nothing
texts.fruit: the fruit, exactly as Rumi says: what a teacher actually transmits. The charlatan of the tradition is judged by the tradition's OWN test

texts.title: The Mafioso
texts.author: Niccolò Masciara
texts.where: Penguin; and 'Palermo: A Thousand-Year-Old City' (Bompiani) for the economics
texts.teaches: what it is like inside, and -- the part that generalises -- why it does not work as a system
texts.fruit: the system. Masciara shows the machine has no succession, no scale, and no exit, and that is why it cannot be copied

texts.title: The Adventures of Don Quixote
texts.author: Miguel de Cervantes
texts.teaches: the greatest novel ever written about a man who cannot tell a genuine authority from a fraud -- and the man who can
texts.fruit: the two of them together. Quixote mistakes a fake knight for a real one; Sancho names the fraud instantly. The book IS the detector and its control

texts.title: The Life and Adventures of Nicholas Nickleby
texts.author: Charles Dickens
texts.teaches: the swindlers of the fair, and Mr. Turveydrop, who teaches a fraud with complete confidence
texts.fruit: the confidence of the fraud. Turveydrop is convincing because of the conviction, not the content

texts.title: The Confessions of a Magnetizer (and the fortune-telling literature around it)
texts.author: various; with Pascal's Pensées on the mechanism
texts.status: public domain (Pascal and the period literature)
texts.where: Pascal's Pensées, art. 'Against the fortune-tellers'; Project Gutenberg
texts.teaches: the actual MECHANISM of the fortune-teller: not mysticism but the law of averages, and why it works on the ones who must believe it
texts.fruit: the arithmetic. Pascal gives the law of averages and it demolishes the whole trade in a paragraph

texts.title: The Criminal Mind
texts.author: Albert D. Cohen
texts.where: the psychiatric account -- usable because it is about the MAN and not the crime
texts.teaches: the criminal as a person rather than a category, and the legal machinery that treats him as a category
texts.fruit: the man's character, over the crime. Cohen's point is that the crime is a symptom, so the fruit is whether the man is treatable

texts.title: The Construction of Social Reality
texts.author: John R. Searle
texts.where: and 'On Liberty' (Mill, 1859, public domain) for the harm principle
texts.teaches: how reality is manufactured, and WHY it can be -- the social construction of the obvious
texts.fruit: the construction. Searle shows that what is taken as given is a thing that was made, and a made thing can be unmade by whoever has the authority

texts.title: The Anatomy of a Scam (the advance-fee tradition, from the Nigerian-letter literature onward)
texts.author: the tradition itself, plus the postal and financial fraud literature
texts.status: public domain for the period literature
texts.where: Project Gutenberg (the confidence-game and postal-fraud literature); the FBI and FTC advisories for the modern forms
texts.teaches: the advance-fee structure: the promise, the small asking, the escalating ask, and the reason it works on the greedy rather than the stupid
texts.fruit: the small ask. Every advance-fee scam begins with a request small enough to seem harmless, and that is the point at which it can be caught

texts.title: A Tale of a Tub
texts.author: Jonathan Swift
texts.teaches: the swindler who is never caught, and the political version of him, which is worse
texts.fruit: the absence of a detector. Swift's swindlers operate in a world where nobody catches them, and the text is the warning

texts.title: The Technological Society
texts.author: Jacques Ellul
texts.teaches: the false need, and the machinery that manufactures it so that asking whether you need it feels naive
texts.fruit: the need's absence. Ellul shows the need is manufactured first and felt second

fruit_tests.name: ends
fruit_tests.question: does what was taken or built still stand, and who benefits from it standing?
fruit_tests.failure: a fake ends in nothing; a real one compounds

fruit_tests.name: transmission
fruit_tests.question: did anything actually transfer -- a capacity, a discernment, a method -- or only words?
fruit_tests.failure: words with no transfer is the charlatan's only product

fruit_tests.name: cost
fruit_tests.question: what did it cost the speaker, in position, in money, in risk?
fruit_tests.failure: a scheme that costs the speaker nothing was never a scheme but a speech

fruit_tests.name: correction
fruit_tests.question: does it survive being checked, and does the checker get a reply?
fruit_tests.failure: an authority that cannot be checked is not an authority, it is a posture

fruit_tests.name: the_others
fruit_tests.question: do the people who know it best endorse it, and have they paid to endorse it?

fruit_tests.name: the_records
fruit_tests.question: is there a record, and does the record include the failures?
fruit_tests.failure: a record of only successes is advertising
